title: Students and opposition parties protest in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner
seoTitle: Delhi protests against CEC Gyanesh Kumar

summary: Students and opposition parties have been protesting in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Election Commission since October 2. Organized by groups including the INDIA bloc, Aam Aadmi Party, All India Students’ Association, and National Students’ Union of India, the protests allege irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and question the commission's functioning. Protesters demand Kumar's resignation, greater transparency in electoral processes, and the use of ballot papers. Delhi Police detained nearly 1,000 people on October 3 and filed multiple FIRs for violating prohibitory orders. A CISF constable was reported to have sustained a minor injury on October 5. Security has been heightened for a scheduled march by opposition MPs to the Election Commission on October 6.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Restoration of eligible voters among deleted names
Use of electoral rolls prepared before Special Intensive Revision (SIR) in future elections
response: Delhi Police have detained nearly 1,000 protesters on October 3 and filed at least three FIRs for violating prohibitory orders, stating that no permission was granted for the protests. Security has been heightened around protest sites and the Election Commission headquarters.

updates.text: Several protesters and political leaders were detained near Jantar Mantar ahead of a proposed demonstration.
Delhi Police detained nearly 1,000 people near Jantar Mantar and filed at least three FIRs for violating prohibitory orders.
All India Students’ Association activists staged demonstrations, with over 150 protesters detained.
A CISF constable sustained a minor injury after being allegedly attacked by a protester during a National Students’ Union of India protest.
Security was heightened around Jantar Mantar and the Election Commission headquarters ahead of a scheduled march by opposition parties.
